Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testIterateJDOM` calls `doTestIterate` that presumably uses JXPathContext's iteratePointers method to iterate over XML elements with namespaces. The current bug report describes that when there are multiple prefixes bound to the same namespace URI, `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` returns the same element multiple times (for the first prefix) and misses elements bound to other prefixes with the same namespace URI.

The core problem is handling multiple prefixes that share the same namespace URI correctly in namespace resolution. The `NamespaceResolver` class is involved in managing namespace URIs and prefixes. From the snippet of `JDOMNodePointer.getNamespaceResolver()`, we see it creates and returns a `NamespaceResolver` holding a namespace context pointer, suggesting this class handles mapping between prefixes and URIs.

The bug arises because the namespace resolver likely only stores or recognizes one prefix per URI (probably the last or first added), so when iterating pointers by XPath queries, it does not correctly recognize elements with different prefixes bound to the same URI as distinct and thus misses them or duplicates others.

This conclusion is reinforced by the first recent bug report describing a regression related to `NamespaceResolver` that broke existing test cases due to wiping the reverse mapping cache on new mappings and preferring the last added prefix.

Hence the incorrect behavior in `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` stems from faulty or incomplete handling of multiple prefixes for a single namespace URI in the `NamespaceResolver` class, leading to incomplete or incorrect XPath iteration results in XML documents with multiple prefixes for the same namespace.

The failing test exercise this scenario with the JDOM model, and the bug manifests with duplicated or missing elements during pointer iteration.

Suggested next step is to inspect how `NamespaceResolver` manages prefix-to-URI and URI-to-prefix mappings, ensuring it supports multiple prefixes per URI correctly, and that `iteratePointers` uses this to include all matching elements rather than filtering or duplicating incorrectly.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
